concepts.name: Client-server request-response model
concepts.summary: Explain that a client sends a request to a server, which returns exactly one response, and that HTTP is initiated by the client.

concepts.name: URL structure
concepts.summary: Recall the parts of a URL: scheme, host, port, path, query string and fragment.

concepts.name: Request methods GET and POST
concepts.summary: Describe that GET retrieves a resource while POST submits data for processing.

concepts.name: Message anatomy
concepts.summary: Describe that a message has a start line, header fields and an optional body.

concepts.name: Status code classes
concepts.summary: Recall that 2xx means success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error and 5xx server error, and know 200, 404 and 500.

concepts.name: HTTP versus HTTPS
concepts.summary: Explain that HTTPS is HTTP carried over an encrypted connection that protects data from eavesdropping.

misconceptions.text: HTTP and the Internet or the web are the same thing.
A 404 status code means the server is down.
POST is secure because the data is not shown in the URL.

concepts.name: Common request headers
concepts.summary: Read and set headers such as Host, User-Agent, Accept and Authorization to shape a request.

concepts.name: Content-Type and body encoding
concepts.summary: Match Content-Type and Content-Length to bodies such as form data, JSON and HTML.

concepts.name: Method semantics PUT DELETE
concepts.summary: Choose among GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and HEAD for a given operation on a resource.

concepts.name: Redirects with Location
concepts.summary: Follow and produce 301, 302 and 307/308 redirects using the Location header.

concepts.name: Cookies basics
concepts.summary: Use Set-Cookie and Cookie to keep state such as a session across stateless requests.

concepts.name: Inspecting traffic with tools
concepts.summary: Use curl and browser developer tools to view and send requests and read responses.

concepts.name: Query strings and parameters
concepts.summary: Encode parameters in the query string with percent-encoding and read them on the server side.

misconceptions.text: Cookies are programs that can run on the user's computer.
Any redirect status code behaves the same way and preserves the method.

concepts.name: Safe and idempotent methods
concepts.summary: Analyse which methods are safe or idempotent and what that implies for retries and caches.

concepts.name: Cache validation with ETag
concepts.summary: Use ETag, Last-Modified and conditional headers to get 304 Not Modified responses.

concepts.name: Cache-Control directives
concepts.summary: Analyse how max-age, no-cache, no-store, public and private determine what may be cached and for how long.

concepts.name: Cookie attributes and sessions
concepts.summary: Analyse how Domain, Path, Expires, Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite affect scope and security of session cookies.

concepts.name: TLS handshake and certificates
concepts.summary: Trace how TLS negotiates keys and how certificates and authorities authenticate the server.

concepts.name: Connection management
concepts.summary: Explain persistent connections and their effect on latency compared with a new connection per request.

concepts.name: Content negotiation and compression
concepts.summary: Use Accept headers and Content-Encoding to select representation, language and compression.

concepts.name: Diagnosing 4xx and 5xx errors
concepts.summary: Distinguish 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 502 and 503 and locate the likely fault from traces.

misconceptions.text: no-cache means the response is never stored.
HttpOnly cookies protect against all cross-site attacks.
Idempotent means the response is the same every time.

concepts.name: HTTP/2 multiplexing
concepts.summary: Analyse how HTTP/2 streams, binary framing and header compression remove HTTP/1.1 head-of-line blocking at the HTTP layer.

concepts.name: HTTP/3 over QUIC
concepts.summary: Compare HTTP/3 over QUIC and UDP with HTTP/2 over TCP regarding loss, handshake and connection migration.

concepts.name: CORS and same-origin policy
concepts.summary: Analyse how the same-origin policy and CORS headers and preflights govern cross-origin browser requests.

concepts.name: Authentication schemes
concepts.summary: Evaluate Basic, bearer token and cookie-based authentication for their security tradeoffs.

concepts.name: Web security headers
concepts.summary: Judge the protection provided by HSTS, CSP and related headers against threats such as downgrade and injection.

concepts.name: Proxies and intermediaries
concepts.summary: Analyse how proxies, load balancers and gateways alter requests, using Forwarded and X-Forwarded-For.

concepts.name: Caching strategy with CDNs
concepts.summary: Evaluate cache layers, Vary, and invalidation approaches such as fingerprinted URLs for a given site.

misconceptions.text: CORS protects the server from unauthorised requests.
HTTP/2 makes all head-of-line blocking disappear.
HTTPS alone makes a web application secure.

concepts.name: Designing resource APIs
concepts.summary: Design HTTP APIs with coherent resources, method semantics, status codes, pagination and error formats.

concepts.name: API evolution and compatibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate versioning, content negotiation and deprecation strategies for evolving APIs without breaking clients.

concepts.name: Performance optimisation strategy
concepts.summary: Design a delivery strategy combining protocol version, caching, compression, prioritisation and preloading from measured latency.

concepts.name: Request smuggling and desync
concepts.summary: Evaluate how inconsistent parsing of message framing between proxies and servers enables smuggling attacks and how to mitigate them.

concepts.name: Resilient retries and rate limiting
concepts.summary: Design retry, timeout, backoff, idempotency-key and rate-limit behaviour using 429 and Retry-After.

concepts.name: Streaming and real-time delivery
concepts.summary: Evaluate chunked transfer, server-sent events, long polling and WebSocket upgrade for real-time needs.

concepts.name: Protocol standards reasoning
concepts.summary: Judge implementation behaviour against HTTP specifications and resolve ambiguities in real-world interoperability.

misconceptions.text: A RESTful API must use only GET, POST, PUT and DELETE with strict CRUD mapping.
Retrying failed requests is always safe if the client backs off.
Request smuggling is only a flaw in server code, not in how components interact.
